title: Lee et al. 2019 (ERP) — EEG dataset and OpenBMI toolbox for three BCI paradigms: an investigation into BCI illiteracy
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 54 healthy participants performing a P300-based brain-computer interface copy-spelling task using a 36-symbol row-column speller paradigm. The study investigates BCI illiteracy through offline training and online testing phases, with 62 EEG channels and 4 EMG auxiliary channels sampled at 1000 Hz. The dataset includes both training data (1980 trials) and test data (2160 trials) with visual feedback, achieving 96.7% accuracy and identifying an 11.1% BCI illiteracy rate among participants.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a BrainAmp system with 62 channels (Ag/AgCl sensors, standard 1005 montage) sampled at 1000 Hz, referenced to nasion with ground at AFz. Participants performed a copy-spelling task with a 36-symbol row-column speller using random-set presentation and face stimuli. Training involved spelling 'NEURAL NETWORKS AND DEEP LEARNING' (33 characters) and testing involved 'PATTERN RECOGNITION MACHINE LEARNING' (36 characters). Each character received 5 sequences of 12 flashes with an inter-stimulus interval of 135 ms and stimulus onset asynchrony of 215 ms. Classification used Linear Discriminant Analysis with mean amplitude feature extraction.
